name: The Jew who sacrificed at Modin
charge: Sacrificing on the heathen altar at the king’s command
summary: The king’s officers came to Modin to compel the people to revolt and to make them sacrifice, and offered Mattathias rank and rewards if he would be the first to fulfil the king’s commandment (1 Maccabees 2:15-18). Mattathias refused for himself, his sons and his brethren, and while he was still speaking one of the Jews came in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king’s commandment (1 Maccabees 2:19-23). Mattathias was inflamed with zeal, ran, and slew him upon the altar, and pulled the altar down (1 Maccabees 2:24-25).
offenseFull: What makes this case is the timing and the audience. The refusal had just been made publicly, in front of the officers and in front of the men of the city; Mattathias had said out loud that though every nation under the king obeyed him and fell away from the religion of their fathers, he and his house would walk in the covenant of their fathers and would not go from their religion on the right hand or the left (1 Maccabees 2:19-22). The offer that had been refused was the flattery and the price together, that he was an honourable and great man with sons and brethren, that the men of Juda and those left at Jerusalem had already done it, and that silver and gold and many rewards and the friendship of the king were waiting (1 Maccabees 2:17-18). Then this man stepped out in the sight of all and took the terms that had just been turned down (1 Maccabees 2:23). The teaching says a gift destroys the heart (Ecclesiastes 7:7), and that a man is not to lay his hand with another man’s sin but to keep himself pure (1 Timothy 5:22); this man did in public the very thing the nation had just been told not to do, and gave the officers the example they had come for.

The law does not treat that as a private failure. The man who is found doing wickedly in the sight of the Lord in transgressing his covenant, who has gone and served other gods and worshipped them, is to be brought out and stoned, on the word of two or three witnesses, and the hands of the witnesses are to be first upon him to put him away (Deuteronomy 17:2-7). Where the enticement comes from a brother, a son, a daughter, a wife or a friend, saying let us go and serve other gods, the sentence is the same and the hand of the man who heard it is to be first upon him, so that all Israel hears and fears (Deuteronomy 13:6-10). The altar at Modin was the test case set up in the town precisely so that the rest would follow.
judgmentFull: Mattathias saw it, was inflamed with zeal, and his reins trembled; he could not forbear to show his anger according to judgment, and he ran and slew the man upon the altar, and the king’s commissioner who compelled men to sacrifice he killed at that time also, and the altar he pulled down (1 Maccabees 2:24-25). The writer gives the precedent in the same breath: thus he dealt zealously for the law of God, as Phinees did to Zambri the son of Salom (1 Maccabees 2:26). Phinees rose up from among the congregation, took a javelin in his hand, and thrust both of them through, and the plague was stayed, and he was given the covenant of an everlasting priesthood because he was zealous for his God and made an atonement for the children of Israel (Numbers 25:7-8; Numbers 25:11-13).

The execution was not the end of the day but the beginning of the revolt. Mattathias cried through the city with a loud voice that whoever was zealous of the law and maintained the covenant should follow him, and he and his sons left everything they had in the city and fled into the mountains (1 Maccabees 2:27-28). The teaching reads the whole scene as one lesson about company: the father’s last charge to his sons was to take to themselves all those that observe the law, because the men around you are what decides whether the work stands, and the man on the altar at Modin is the other kind. One man taking the reward in front of everybody was what the king’s policy needed, and the answer to it set the nation in motion.

lawsResolved.text: Anyone that has served or worshipped false or pagan gods shall be put to death.
He that sacrifices to any god, other than the LORD God alone, shall be utterly destroyed.
Death penalty is to be given to idolaters.

text.text: In the mean while the king’s officers, such as compelled the people to revolt, came into the city Modin, to make them sacrifice.
And when many of Israel came unto them, Mattathias also and his sons came together.
Then answered the king’s officers, and said to Mattathias on this wise, Thou art a ruler, and an honourable and great man in this city, and strengthened with sons and brethren:

Now therefore come thou first, and fulfil the king’s commandment, like as all the heathen have done, yea, and the men of Juda also, and such as remain at Jerusalem: so shalt thou and thy house be in the number of the king’s friends, and thou and thy children shall be honoured with silver and gold, and many rewards.

Then Mattathias answered and spake with a loud voice, Though all the nations that are under the king’s dominion obey him, and fall away every one from the religion of their fathers, and give consent to his commandments:
Yet will I and my sons and my brethren walk in the covenant of our fathers.
God forbid that we should forsake the law and the ordinances.
We will not hearken to the king’s words, to go from our religion, either on the right hand, or the left.
Surely oppression maketh a wise man mad; and a gift destroyeth the heart.
Lay hands suddenly on no man, neither be partaker of other men’s sins: keep thyself pure.
Now when he had left speaking these words, there came one of the Jews in the sight of all to sacrifice on the altar which was at Modin, according to the king’s commandment.
Which thing when Mattathias saw, he was inflamed with zeal, and his reins trembled, neither could he forbear to shew his anger according to judgment: wherefore he ran, and slew him upon the altar.
Also the king’s commissioner, who compelled men to sacrifice, he killed at that time, and the altar he pulled down.
Thus dealt he zealously for the law of God like as Phinees did unto Zambri the son of Salom.
And Mattathias cried throughout the city with a loud voice, saying, Whosoever is zealous of the law, and maintaineth the covenant, let him follow me.
So he and his sons fled into the mountains, and left all that ever they had in the city.
If there be found among you, within any of thy gates which the Lord thy God giveth thee, man or woman, that hath wrought wickedness in the sight of the Lord thy God, in transgressing his covenant,
And hath gone and served other gods, and worshipped them, either the sun, or moon, or any of the host of heaven, which I have not commanded;
And it be told thee, and thou hast heard of it, and enquired diligently, and, behold, it be true, and the thing certain, that such abomination is wrought in Israel:
Then shalt thou bring forth that man or that woman, which have committed that wicked thing, unto thy gates, even that man or that woman, and shalt stone them with stones, till they die.
At the mouth of two witnesses, or three witnesses, shall he that is worthy of death be put to death; but at the mouth of one witness he shall not be put to death.
The hands of the witnesses shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterward the hands of all the people. So thou shalt put the evil away from among you.

If thy brother, the son of thy mother, or thy son, or thy daughter, or the wife of thy bosom, or thy friend, which is as thine own soul, entice thee secretly, saying, Let us go and serve other gods, which thou hast not known, thou, nor thy fathers;
Namely, of the gods of the people which are round about you, nigh unto thee, or far off from thee, from the one end of the earth even unto the other end of the earth;
Thou shalt not consent unto him, nor hearken unto him; neither shall thine eye pity him, neither shalt thou spare, neither shalt thou conceal him:
But thou shalt surely kill him; thine hand shall be first upon him to put him to death, and afterwards the hand of all the people.
And thou shalt stone him with stones, that he die; because he hath sought to thrust thee away from the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage.
And when Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, saw it, he rose up from among the congregation, and took a javelin in his hand;
And he went after the man of Israel into the tent, and thrust both of them through, the man of Israel, and the woman through her belly. So the plague was stayed from the children of Israel.

Phinehas, the son of Eleazar, the son of Aaron the priest, hath turned my wrath away from the children of Israel, while he was zealous for my sake among them, that I consumed not the children of Israel in my jealousy.
Wherefore say, Behold, I give unto him my covenant of peace:
And he shall have it, and his seed after him, even the covenant of an everlasting priesthood; because he was zealous for his God, and made an atonement for the children of Israel.
Take also unto you all those that observe the law, and avenge ye the wrong of your people.
